title: Task-Efficient Agent Evaluation Using Cached Traces
title_zh: 利用缓存轨迹实现任务高效的智能体评估

paragraphs.en: Efficient benchmarking estimates a system’s full benchmark performance from a small number of task executions. Standard approaches rely solely on the binary correctness of executions from a collection of already-evaluated reference systems. An agentic system, however, produces a rich trace for each execution that can reveal substantially more about its capabilities. Leveraging this information requires useful trace representations. We propose representing a trace by extracting a structured summary of it with an LLM and embedding the summary with a standard text encoder. These representations preserve correctness- and task-related signal while minimizing the presence of system identity-, model family-, and harness-related signals that dominate raw trace embeddings. Given this representation for each task execution from all reference systems, we construct low-dimensional representations of the systems and predict a new system’s score from its position among the reference systems. On SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench 2.0, augmenting an item-response model with this geometry-based prediction reduces mean absolute error from 0.13 to 0.08 (Wilcoxon p < 10 − 4 p<10^{-4} ) and from 0.14 to 0.12 (Wilcoxon p < 10 − 3 p<10^{-3} ), respectively, when provided a single random executed task. Further, given access to the full set of reference systems, our approach dominates baselines for any given number of executed tasks on both benchmarks.

paragraphs.en: Generative model use is increasingly agentic: systems plan, invoke tools, observe intermediate results, and iterate over long horizons to complete complex tasks ( Yang et al., 2024 ; Wang and others, 2025 ) . As agentic capabilities increase, so does the range of settings in which a given system might be deployed – and, with it, the number of benchmarks on which the system must be evaluated before it can be trusted with consequential work ( Kapoor et al., 2026 ) . Agentic evaluation, however, is expensive. Each task execution requires a properly sandboxed environment and routinely consumes hundreds of thousands of tokens ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ; Merrill et al., 2026 ) . Full evaluation on a benchmark can regularly exceed $2,000 ( Kapoor et al., 2026 ) . Given this cost, efficient evaluation is necessary to improve the evaluation coverage of an agentic system.

paragraphs.en: Task-efficient evaluation methods address this problem by finding structure in item-level information available from previously evaluated reference systems to mitigate the cost of evaluating a new system. Some task-efficient evaluation methods require only the item-level scores from reference systems ( Maia Polo et al., 2024 ; Vivek et al., 2024 ; Kipnis et al., 2025 ; Bowyer et al., 2026 ) . Others leverage information in cached artifacts, such as natural language responses ( Acharyya et al., 2024 ; Helm et al., 2025 ) or residual streams ( Duderstadt et al., 2023 ) , to measure the similarity of systems on a set of tasks. Agentic workflows often produce artifacts when executing a task – file diffs, tool calls, intermediate plans, and error messages – recorded together in an execution trace that can be used to this effect. Existing methods for using cached artifacts rely on off-the-shelf embedding functions that typically capture system or model idiosyncrasies ( Sun et al., 2025 ) better than trace functionality. Along these lines, we make two primary contributions:

paragraphs.en: Task-efficient evaluation using cached traces. Given the trubric embeddings from a set of tasks for a target system and a collection of reference systems, we evaluate their utility for predicting the target system’s full benchmark score on SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench 2.0 under three different agentic system evaluation protocols. We find that trubric -based estimators, combined with an item-response model, reduce single task mean absolute error from 0.13 to 0.08 ( p < 10 − 4 p<10^{-4} ) and from 0.14 to 0.12 ( p < 10 − 3 p<10^{-3} ) on the two benchmarks, respectively, and are nearly always better than baselines at every task budget (Table 1 ).

paragraphs.en: The standard tools for embedding model artifacts are text encoders trained on sentence-level semantic similarity ( Reimers and Gurevych, 2019 ; Su et al., 2023 ; Nussbaum and Duderstadt, 2025 ) . Agentic traces, however, implicitly or explicitly encode system metadata that may not be relevant for downstream tasks ( Sun et al., 2025 ; Oderinwale, 2026 ) and are therefore not necessarily encoded well by semantic embedding models. Instead, traces have primarily been studied through taxonomies of failure modes and actions ( Cemri et al., 2025 ; Shu et al., 2026 ) and LLM judges ( Zhuge et al., 2025 ; Mehtiyev and Assunção, 2026 ) . Parallel work uses LLMs to adapt outputs to be more naturally compared via their semantics ( Ravfogel et al., 2024 ; Peng et al., 2024 ; Benara et al., 2024 ) . trubric applies this to agentic traces by embedding a task-specific structured summary of each trace.

paragraphs.en: Task-efficient benchmarking estimates a system’s full benchmark score from a small number of executions. The dominant paradigm for efficient benchmarking centers around item response theory (IRT) ( Birnbaum, 1968 ) , where a target system’s score is estimated with m ≤ M m\leq M item-level scores by assigning a latent ability based on the relationship between a task’s difficulty and discriminability ( Maia Polo et al., 2024 ; Kipnis et al., 2025 ) . Extensions of IRT select informative or adaptive task subsets ( Vivek et al., 2024 ; Truong et al., 2025 ) . A complementary paradigm represents the systems themselves, either from their score profiles ( Ruan et al., 2024 ; Zhuang et al., 2025 ) or from the artifacts they produce while executing a task ( Duderstadt et al., 2023 ; Acharyya et al., 2024 ; Helm et al., 2025 ) . For example, the Product Kernel Perspective Space (PKPS) ( Helm et al., 2026a ) represents language models as Euclidean objects obtained via multidimensional scaling of the distances between their embedded responses. Helm et al. (2026b) regress benchmark scores on similar representations and prove that the estimate is task-efficient relative to the sample score. trubric enables extending geometry-based methods to agentic systems by providing an effective trace encoding. We show that these two approaches – score-based IRT and trace-based PKPS – can be combined to outperform either constituent for any given number of executed tasks when the full set of reference systems is available.

paragraphs.en: A trace representation for benchmark prediction should place two traces close together when they reflect similar execution behavior on a task. Concretely, we consider five attributes of a trace that a representation might encode: (i) task (i.e., which task the trace corresponds to), (ii) correctness (i.e., whether the trace produced a correct output), (iii) system identity (i.e., which system produced the trace), (iv) model family (i.e., the family of the underlying generative model), and (v) harness (i.e., the harness used to produce the trace). For efficient benchmarking with traces, an ideal representation encodes (i) and (ii) but not (iii)–(v). trubric constructs such a representation in two stages.

paragraphs.en: To quantify what a trace representation encodes, we train balanced linear classifiers to predict each of the five attributes of Section 3.1 for a held-out trace from its embedding. Classifiers for the system-level attributes (iii)–(v) are evaluated on held-out tasks. Classifiers for (i) and (ii) are evaluated on held-out groups of systems. We evaluate trace representations using the cached SWE-bench Verified traces and report balanced accuracy for each attribute. Higher accuracy is preferred for attributes (i) and (ii). Near chance accuracy is preferred for attributes (iii)–(v). Detailed descriptions of the classification tasks are provided in Appendix A.2 .

paragraphs.en: We compare trubric embeddings to two baseline representations: raw trace , which uses g g to embed the start and end of each trace, and generic , which follows the two-stage construction of Section 3.1 with fixed field descriptions in place of a task-specific rubric. Unless otherwise stated, both the generic and trubric representations use K = 6 K=6 fields, with DeepSeek-V4-Flash ( DeepSeek-AI, 2026 ) as both the rubric generator and summarizer. For the embedding function g g , we consider seven text encoders: text-embedding-3-small ( Neelakantan et al., 2022 ) , nomic-embed-text-v1.5 ( Nussbaum et al., 2025 ) , bge-large-en-v1.5 ( Xiao et al., 2024 ) , gte-large ( Li et al., 2023 ) , e5-large-v2 ( Wang et al., 2022 ) , all-mpnet-base-v2 , and all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ( Reimers and Gurevych, 2019 ) . These encoders span open- and closed-source models, multiple architectures and training procedures, and embedding dimension sizes. The prompts and fixed field descriptions are provided in Appendix A.3 .

paragraphs.en: Modern leaderboards contain many entries that share an underlying model or harness. To emulate the process of evaluating a new model or harness, as well as a new combination of the two, we consider three different evaluation protocols: leave-one-system-out where only the target itself is excluded from the references, leave-one-family-out where references whose underlying model family matches the target’s are additionally excluded, and leave-one-harness-out where references sharing the target’s harness are excluded. Detailed descriptions of a system’s assignment to a model family or harness are provided in Appendix C .
paragraphs.zh: 现代排行榜中包含许多条目，它们共享同一个底层模型或评测框架。 为了模拟评估新模型或新评测框架，以及两者新组合的过程，我们考虑三种不同的评估协议：留一系统法（leave-one-system-out），即仅将目标本身从参考中排除；留一模型族法（leave-one-family-out），即额外排除底层模型族与目标相同的参考；留一评测框架法（leave-one-harness-out），即排除与目标共享同一评测框架的参考。 关于智能体系统被归入某个模型族或评测框架的详细说明见附录 C。

paragraphs.en: For each task budget m m , we consider two methods for selecting the target’s m m executed tasks. Random selection draws the m m tasks uniformly. Reported results average over 50 randomly sampled task subsets. Adaptive selection chooses tasks greedily using the fitted item-response model. In particular at each step, the task with the highest expected Fisher information under the current ability posterior is executed and the posterior is updated (Appendix B ).

paragraphs.en: The differences in attributes (i)–(v) are also reflected in the quality of the system-level geometry for predicting benchmark score. Figure 2 shows a stronger relationship between system position in the embedding space and benchmark score for trubric than for raw-trace embeddings. paragraphs.en: Table 1 and Figure 3 show that trubric -based geometry predicts full benchmark performance more accurately than the sample score for small task budgets ( m ≤ 10 m\leq 10 ) and the population mean for all budgets. The trubric -based geometry can also outperform IRT, which exploits the correctness patterns of reference systems, at small task budgets. On SWE-bench, the geometry produces a more accurate estimate from 1 through 10 random tasks (Figure 3 ). On Terminal-Bench, y ^ geom \hat{y}_{\mathrm{geom}} outperforms IRT at one task, but y ^ IRT \hat{y}_{\mathrm{IRT}} is more accurate from three tasks onward. We emphasize that the geometric methods only require the target’s trace content, and not its correctness labels, which means that these methods are applicable in settings where grading target tasks is infeasible (e.g., due to cost, lack of expertise, etc.), provided scored reference systems are available. y ^ geom \hat{y}_{\mathrm{geom}} can be interpreted as a high-bias, low-variance estimate of the full benchmark score.

paragraphs.en: The trace-based predictions and correctness-based predictions exhibit different behavior as the task budget grows: trace-based predictions are informative with very few executions, while IRT improves substantially as the number of tasks increases. Figure 3 shows that combining their predictions improves prediction across all evaluated budgets and benchmarks. At m = 5 m=5 on SWE-bench, IRT + + trubric achieves 0.063 MAE, compared with 0.069 for geometry alone (Wilcoxon’s p < 10 − 4 p<10^{-4} ) and 0.088 for IRT (Wilcoxon’s p < 10 − 12 p<10^{-12} ). On Terminal-Bench – where IRT is relatively stronger – the combination achieves 0.090, compared with 0.107 for geometry (Wilcoxon’s p < 10 − 3 p<10^{-3} ) and 0.097 for IRT (Wilcoxon’s p < 10 − 2 p<10^{-2} ). These results suggest a complementary predictive value of execution artifacts and correctness outcomes. The broad pattern persists across the system-, family-, and harness-exclusion protocols in Figure 3 , although the size of the improvement varies.

paragraphs.en: The left panel of Figure 4 shows that increasing the number of reference systems generally improves both IRT and geometry-based estimators. At m = 5 m=5 random tasks on SWE-bench, expanding from n = 20 n=20 to n = 107 n=107 reduces geometry-only MAE from 0.086 to 0.069 and IRT + + trubric MAE from 0.081 to 0.063. paragraphs.en: Figure 5 translates the error curves into the cost of evaluating a system. paragraphs.en: We also evaluate methods for comparing two systems head to head. For each pair of systems whose true benchmark scores differ by at least 0.05, we exclude both systems from the references and ask whether an estimator correctly identifies the better system from m m random executions per system (right two panels of Figure 5 ). On SWE-bench, IRT + + trubric decides 88% of pairs correctly from a single task per system, compared with 79% for IRT and 69% for the sample score. By five tasks per system, all estimators exceed 90% and the score-based estimators are competitive or better. On Terminal-Bench, IRT is the most accurate estimator at every tested budget. Trace information is thus most valuable for head-to-head comparisons in the lowest budget regime, where executing a single task per system ($4 for the pair) identifies the better system in nearly nine of ten pairs.
paragraphs.zh: 我们还评估了将两个系统进行正面对比的方法。 对于真实基准分数相差至少 0.05 的每一对系统，我们将这两个系统从参考集合中排除，并检验估计器能否从每个系统 m m 次随机执行中正确识别出更好的系统（图 5 的右侧两个面板）。 在 SWE-bench 上，IRT++trubric 在每个系统仅执行单个任务的情况下正确判定 88% 的系统对，相比之下 IRT 为 79%，样本分数为 69%。 当每个系统执行五个任务时，所有估计器都超过 90%，且基于分数的估计器具有竞争力甚至更好。 在 Terminal-Bench 上，IRT 是在所有测试预算下最准确的估计器。 因此，轨迹信息在最低预算区间内的正面对比中最有价值，此时每个系统执行单个任务（每对系统 4 美元）就能在近九成的系统对中识别出更好的系统。

paragraphs.en: We introduced trubric , a trace representation constructed by extracting a task-specific structured summary of a trace with an LLM and embedding the summary with a standard text encoder. Across seven text encoders, trubric embeddings preserve information about the task and the correctness of an execution while minimizing idiosyncratic information about the system, model family, and harness that produced it.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 trubric，这是一种轨迹表示方法，通过使用大语言模型从轨迹中提取特定任务的结构化摘要，并用标准文本编码器对该摘要进行嵌入而构建。 在七个文本编码器上，trubric 嵌入能够保留关于任务及其执行正确性的信息，同时最大限度地减少关于产生该轨迹的系统、模型家族与测试框架的特异性信息。

sents.en: We introduced trubric , a trace representation constructed by extracting a task-specific structured summary of a trace with an LLM and embedding the summary with a standard text encoder.
sents.zh: 我们提出了 trubric，这是一种轨迹表示方法，通过使用大语言模型从轨迹中提取特定任务的结构化摘要，并用标准文本编码器对该摘要进行嵌入而构建。

sents.en: Across seven text encoders, trubric embeddings preserve information about the task and the correctness of an execution while minimizing idiosyncratic information about the system, model family, and harness that produced it.
sents.zh: 在七个文本编码器上，trubric 嵌入能够保留关于任务及其执行正确性的信息，同时最大限度地减少关于产生该轨迹的系统、模型家族与测试框架的特异性信息。

paragraphs.en: We then proposed using trubric embeddings to induce representations of agentic systems for task-efficient evaluation. The resulting geometry supports accurate benchmark score prediction from as little as a single executed task and, combined with an item-response model, is never worse than either constituent at any task budget when the full set of reference systems is available.
paragraphs.zh: 随后我们提出使用基准嵌入（trubric embeddings）来诱导智能体系统的表示，以实现高效任务的评估。 由此得到的几何结构支持仅凭单个已执行任务就能准确预测基准分数，并且在与项目反应模型结合后，只要完整的参考智能体系统集合可用，在任何任务预算下都不会差于任一组成部分。

sents.en: The resulting geometry supports accurate benchmark score prediction from as little as a single executed task and, combined with an item-response model, is never worse than either constituent at any task budget when the full set of reference systems is available.

paragraphs.en: The combined estimator reduces the cost of reaching an MAE below 0.10 on SWE-bench Verified from $10–$40 to $2 per system. These results are relatively robust to the major design choices: the text encoder, the number of rubric fields, and the task selection method. Importantly, these results support the claim that extracting more than binary correctness from cached executions can improve the efficiency of agentic evaluation as the number of systems and benchmarks continues to grow – providing a route toward improved evaluation coverage for a given system.
paragraphs.zh: 组合估计器将在 SWE-bench Verified 上达到低于 0.10 的 MAE 的成本从每个系统 10–40 美元降低到 2 美元。 这些结果对主要设计选择相对稳健：文本编码器、评分准则字段的数量以及任务选择方法。 重要的是，这些结果支持了这样一个论断：从缓存的执行中提取超越二元正确性的更多信息，可以在系统数量和基准测试持续增长的情况下提升智能体评估的效率——为提升给定系统的评估覆盖范围提供了一条途径。

paragraphs.en: We evaluated trubric along the five attributes relevant to efficient evaluation. We make no claims about the usefulness of the representation for other tasks one might consider with traces, such as change detection ( Bridgeford and Helm, 2025 ) , online monitoring ( Helm et al., 2026c ) , early stopping ( Ruan et al., 2026 ; Wang et al., 2026 ) , or steering ( Rahn et al., 2024 ) . We leave the study of trubric -like representations for these tasks to future work.

paragraphs.en: UsernameValidator allows trailing newline in usernames Description ASCIIUsernameValidator and UnicodeUsernameValidator use the regex r’^[\w.@+-]+$’ The intent is to only allow alphanumeric characters as well as ., @, +, and -. However, a little known quirk of Python regexes is that $ will also match a trailing newline. Therefore, the user name validators will accept usernames which end with a newline. You can avoid this behavior by instead using \A and \Z to terminate regexes. For example, the validator regex could be changed to r’\A[\w.@+-]+\Z’ in order to reject usernames that end with a newline. I am not sure how to officially post a patch, but the required change is trivial - using the regex above in the two validators in contrib.auth.validators.
paragraphs.zh: UsernameValidator 允许用户名末尾包含换行符 描述 ASCIIUsernameValidator 和 UnicodeUsernameValidator 使用正则表达式 r’^[\w.@+-]+$’，其意图是仅允许字母数字字符以及 .、@、+ 和 -。 然而，Python 正则表达式有一个鲜为人知的特性：$ 也会匹配末尾的换行符。 因此，这些用户名验证器会接受以换行符结尾的用户名。 可以改用 \A 和 \Z 来终止正则表达式，从而避免这种行为。 例如，可以将验证器的正则表达式改为 r’\A[\w.@+-]+\Z’，以拒绝以换行符结尾的用户名。 我不确定如何正式提交补丁，但所需的修改非常简单——在 contrib.auth.validators 中的两个验证器里使用上述正则表达式即可。

paragraphs.en: We fit the two-parameter logistic model ℙ ⁡ ( s ⁡ ( x i ​ j ) = 1 ) = sigmoid ⁡ ( a j ​ ( θ i − b j ) ) \mathbb{P}(s(x_{ij})=1)=\mathrm{sigmoid}\left(a_{j}(\theta_{i}-b_{j})\right) to the reference score matrix by maximum a posteriori estimation, with standard normal priors on the abilities θ i \theta_{i} and difficulties b j b_{j} and a 𝒩 ⁡ ( 0 , 1 / 10 ) \mathcal{N}(0,1/10) prior on the log-discriminations log ⁡ a j \log a_{j} (centering the slopes at the Rasch value of one), optimized with L-BFGS. Because the benchmark score aggregates tasks beyond the M M -task panel (all 500 tasks for SWE-bench Verified; all tasks and trials for Terminal-Bench 2.0), we additionally fit a monotone link from ability to benchmark score, y ≈ sigmoid ⁡ ( c 1 ​ θ + c 0 ) y\approx\mathrm{sigmoid}(c_{1}\theta+c_{0}) , by least squares on the reference systems.
